column1: Segmentation runs on customer-level *averages* of monthly ratios (Jan-Dec 2025). This smooths out month-to-month volatility, so a customer who was briefly stressed in one month but healthy the rest of the year is not flagged as 'stressed' at this grain.

91 customers (9.1%) have fewer than 12 months of history (e.g. joined mid-year). K-Means correctly isolated most of them into their own cluster(s) rather than forcing them into the two established-customer segments, but their profiles are based on very few data points and should be treated as provisional.

December transaction recency was missing for 81 customers and was imputed with the feature's median before scaling/clustering. This is a reasonable default but slightly compresses the true spread of the recency feature.

All synthetic financial fields (income, credit limit, balances) are inflated relative to real Vietnamese salaries by construction (see case study, Section 7/12). Only ratio-based features were used for clustering and recommendation rules for this reason; no raw VND figures were used as clustering inputs or thresholds.
financial_health_score is a wellbeing indicator, not a credit score. No output of this notebook is used, or should ever be used, to approve, deny, or reprice credit.

K-means with k chosen by silhouette score is one reasonable segmentation method; the silhouette scores in Section 4.5 show a shallow, not razor-sharp, peak at k=4 (see the model-selection chart), so alternative k or algorithms (e.g. Gaussian mixtures, hierarchical clustering) could reasonably produce a different but still defensible split.

Segment names are derived programmatically from cluster statistics (Section 4.8) rather than hand-picked, which improves reproducibility, but the underlying business meaning should still be sanity-checked by a human against a few example customers before it goes on a client-facing slide.

Task 5 driver strength is scored on a separate, non-defining 'evidence_metric' rather than on the feature used to build the target-group mask itself (e.g. Budgeting Tool is defined by spend-to-income but its evidence metric is credit_utilization_ratio). Scoring effect size on the same feature used to define the group would be circular -- a group defined as its own top quartile always shows a large, uninformative effect size on that feature. That same-feature number is still reported in the output table for audit purposes but is not used for ranking.

Clustering features were checked for redundancy first (Section 4.4): category_diversity and spend_to_income_ratio were dropped because they were near-duplicates (|r| >= 0.75) of engagement_score / financial_health_score. credit_utilization_ratio was kept despite a residual r = -0.79 with financial_health_score, since credit-line usage intensity is a meaningfully different lever for the business (a spend-alert/product-suggestion decision) than the composite health score itself; this residual correlation still means the 'financial stress' construct carries somewhat more implicit weight in the clustering distance than a single, fully independent feature would.
